purpose: Dialogue main pixel-art style exploration; in-world running art is called Q/chibi pixel art. All options pending user selection; no production character replacement.

variants.detail: 颗粒鲜明，成年比例，简练色块
variants.style: Authentic hand-placed late-16-bit adventure-game portrait art. Intentionally medium-coarse visible square pixels: imagine each waist-up character designed on a roughly 100 by 150 pixel native grid, then enlarged with nearest-neighbor. Adult anatomical proportions, head about one third of the visible head-to-hip crop, expressive but naturally sized eyes. A deliberately restrained 24-32 color ramp, two to three value planes per material, strong dark colored outlines, economical angular pixel clusters, slight selective dithering. Clear facial likeness using very few expertly chosen clusters. Flat readable forms and graphic rhythm rather than polished smooth rendering. This is substantially more mature and expressive than a chibi walking sprite. Big beautiful visibly crafted pixels, absolutely no smooth painting, gradient shading, random noise or pixelation filter.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a new two-character pixel-art STYLE EXPLORATION image for the main dialogue portraits of the Hamilton narrative game. This is concept selection artwork, not in-world chibi characters. The two attached social-media screenshots in the conversation are NOT desired styles and must NOT be reproduced.
Subjects, keep recognizably distinct:
LEFT: Alexander Hamilton in the original musical's Lin-Manuel Miranda portrayal, warm light-medium complexion, naturally expressive brown eyes, long narrow face, dark brown hair swept back into a LOW ponytail, small mustache and neat goatee, youthful ambitious adult. Navy Continental coat with wide buff lapels and cuffs, cream waistcoat and brass buttons, white stock and cravat, no epaulettes.
RIGHT: Marquis de Lafayette in the original musical's Daveed Diggs portrayal, medium-brown Black complexion, long face, brown eyes, black curly hair gathered into a HIGH curly bun, neatly trimmed full short beard, confident gracious adult. Deep navy officer coat, gold fringed epaulettes, pale cream lapels and waistcoat, brass buttons, white stock/cravat.
Composition: a landscape 3:2 canvas with EXACTLY TWO separate upper-body portraits side by side. Consistent adult proportions for both: if bodies were completed they would be about 6.5-7 heads tall. Both shown from complete hair top to upper thighs, same scale with equal head sizes and an aligned waistline; generous small outer margins and a clear empty gap between people. Hamilton on the left turns 25 degrees inward toward the right; Lafayette on the right turns 25 degrees inward toward the left. Both faces remain clearly readable in gentle three-quarter view, not profiles. Both upright, thoughtful closed-mouth attentive expression, relaxed arms with hands lightly resting near the waist, no crossing arms, no props. Entire hair, heads and elbows inside image.
Backdrop: one uniform matte warm-light parchment gray #e7e2d6, perfectly flat, no scenery, no texture, no shadows cast onto backdrop. No UI, no framing card, no lettering, no title, no labels, no typography, no watermark. Both characters equally visible and lit; no inactive-character darkening in this style comparison.
This image must demonstrate one cohesive art direction consistently across BOTH characters. Draw original new artwork. Prioritize beautiful intentional pixel design and recognizable distinct faces.

variants.detail: 五官清楚、轮廓利落，细节与像素感均衡
variants.style: Sophisticated 32-bit narrative-RPG dialogue portrait pixel art, roughly 180 by 260 native pixels per head-to-hip figure. Adult anatomical proportions with a subtly expressive face, head about one third of the head-to-hip crop, no chibi, no enormous anime eyes. Clean restrained colored outlines, finely planned pixel clusters, 48-64-color controlled palette, elegant cel-like facial planes, 4-5 tones per material. Hair is grouped into readable angular locks, coat lapels and buttons are precise, eyebrows and mouths carry nuanced character. Warm approachable storytelling energy, flattering even key light with moderate contrast. The happy midpoint between obvious square-pixel craft and detailed expressive portrait illustration. Every contour and highlight has visible deliberate square-pixel stepping. No smooth painted airbrush, no 3D render and no pseudo-pixel photo filter.

variants.detail: 弱描边、柔和色块，偏安静的历史插画
variants.style: Painterly pixel-art historical character portraits, adult realistic anatomy, visible square pixel clusters on a roughly 230 by 340 native grid per head-to-hip character. Quiet atmospheric storybook treatment: no black comic outline, lost-and-found colored contour edges, warm muted ochres and desaturated indigo, broad rhythmic pixel masses in hair and cloth, restrained elegant selective dithering, artfully simplified faces with nuanced natural expressions. Soft-edged form is constructed from STEPPED SQUARE PIXEL CLUSTERS not antialiased strokes. Low-to-medium contrast, warm diffuse light, gentle color transitions made from small distinct palette steps. Cloth folds feel painted with flat pixel mosaics and broad color masses; do not add microtexture. Mood is intimate, literary and humane. Must remain unmistakable pixel art when viewed at normal scale. Not chibi, not anime, not a smooth oil painting with a pixel filter.

variants.detail: 五官、发丝、衣料最细，明暗对比强
variants.style: High-definition cinematic pixel-art dialogue portraits with adult realistic anatomy and strong facial likeness, about 320 by 460 native pixel design per head-to-hip character. Rich but meticulously organized fine square pixels, sculpted cheekbones, individually grouped hair strands, fine embroidery and brass button glints, detailed coat folds and believable fabric material, selective broken contours rather than thick outline. Directional warm stage-like key light and cool indigo shadow planes create dramatic volume, while preserving complete face legibility. High contrast, sophisticated deep navy / buff / gold palette and precise fine pixel accents. This is the upper end of detail density for a pixel-art portrait: more dimensional and nuanced than retro sprite work, still DELIBERATE stepped square pixels across the image, never a photograph or 3D render filtered into pixels. No chibi or anime eyes.
